codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of initializeDefaultItems() in the Zustand promotion store. All 4 default How to Shop items and 4 default Important Notes items match the original vanilla JS app exactly (promotion-ui.js lines 2193-2253). Profile data integration (storePhone, storeEmail) is correctly wired via the profile helper functions. The empty-array guard correctly prevents overwriting saved state. Store directions logic faithfully reproduces the original ensureStoreDirectionsImportantNote() deduplication check. Called after loadFromIndexedDB() in PromotionPage mount with proper async/await handling. 11 comprehensive tests cover all expected behaviors including fresh state, saved state preservation, profile data, unique IDs, and formatting flags.

issues.description: Behavioral divergence from original app: the original vanilla JS app calls ensureStoreDirectionsImportantNote() unconditionally on load (promotion-ui.js:762), meaning directions are added even when saved important notes already exist. The React implementation only adds directions inside initializeDefaultItems() when importantNotesItems is empty. If a user has saved important notes but later adds directions to their profile, the directions note won't appear. This matches the feature spec ('populates defaults only when the arrays are empty') but diverges from the original app's behavior. A separate ensureStoreDirectionsImportantNote() call in the mount useEffect would restore parity.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The original vanilla JS app has a two-step pattern on load: initializeDefaultItems() (only populates empty arrays) followed by ensureStoreDirectionsImportantNote() (unconditionally adds directions note if missing). The React migration collapsed both into initializeDefaultItems(), losing the unconditional directions check. This is a subtle behavioral difference that should be documented in architecture.md or addressed in a follow-up feature.

summary: Feature passes review. The implementation correctly restores default How to Shop and Important Notes items matching the original vanilla JS app, with proper profile data integration and saved-state preservation. One non-blocking behavioral divergence was noted: the original app unconditionally checks for directions notes on load (separate from default population), while the React implementation only checks during default population. All 82 tests pass including 11 new ones with thorough coverage.
